back: A crop that completes its life cycle from seed to seed in one season, e.g. maize, beans.
A crop that needs two seasons to flower and set seed; harvested after the first, e.g. onion, carrot, cabbage.
A crop that lives for more than two years, e.g. citrus, mango, banana, sugar cane.
Mono: one cotyledon, parallel veins, fibrous roots, scattered bundles. Di: two cotyledons, net veins, tap root, bundles in a ring.

front: Which part of the Irish potato is eaten?
back: A stem tuber (it has eyes, which are buds).
Tomato, Irish potato, tobacco (also pepper, eggplant).
Crops in one family share pests and diseases; changing family breaks their cycles. Legumes also leave nitrogen for the next crop.
Cereals, legumes, roots and tubers, fruits (plus vegetables and industrial crops such as cotton and tobacco).
